# Copying: what the combined evidence establishes

Updated 2026-10-08. **A learned longer-copy repair is demonstrated, and its training sites are partly localized.** Combined positional exposure succeeds in every fresh confirmation seed in two successive comparisons. Cross-only exposure succeeds in two of the latest three seeds; neither single-site intervention meets the all-seed rule. Shared-checkpoint continuation now shows a substantial exposure benefit after a weak solution has already formed, though incomplete recovery. The learned mediator remains unresolved. This is a bounded account of our small model, not a novel architecture or an explanation of every learned weight.

## Review after the terminal-feedback interventions

2026-10-08. The latest reports and machine-readable criteria were checked together. No new experiment or training was performed for this review.

| Claim | Current evidence | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| A supplied read pattern can recover the failed decision | Head-0 transfer gives 128/128 fifth-token answers; wrong-position control gives 0/128 | Conditional local sufficiency; full copying and proper stopping under transfer remain untested |
| Terminal feedback affects the learned behavior | Matched loss deletion changes answers and the marker pattern | All deletion branches lose long stopping; attention mediation is not isolated |
| Classifier-only terminal learning preserves stopping | Directly tested and rejected under the fixed continuation | Short training fit also collapses; no universal gradient-necessity conclusion |
| Broader positional exposure can learn a complete-copy repair | Earlier combined-exposure confirmation passes its declared groups | Small task/model and bounded position range; the exact learned mechanism remains open |

These results do not establish the complete chain `terminal feedback -> head-0 mismatch -> premature EOS`. They establish separate training effects and one endpoint intervention. Losing the ability to stop can trivially remove premature stopping, so improved content or a smaller attention gap cannot bridge that causal gap.

**Priority decision:** stop modifying terminal feedback. Return to the original same-seed cross-only versus combined-exposure trajectories, where terminal targets remain present and the final combined model fits the complete task. Use existing saved snapshots first. The next question should explain why the successful exposure recipe learns transferable content and stopping together, rather than why a newly restricted recipe fails.

Before launching a new study, specify one candidate mediator and opposite predictions that distinguish it from general EOS suppression. Require content and actual terminal decisions, a control for intervention-induced damage, and complete-copy/short-fit criteria if any training is proposed. Head identities must not be assumed to match by index. Another attention plot, broad component sweep, EOS-weight search or larger budget alone does not meet this gate.

Fresh confirmation is appropriate only after a concrete mechanism or usable repair is specified. The repaired combined-exposure model already exists; a new architecture is not justified by these failed diagnostic continuations. No new run is queued. Detailed methods, primary sources and evidence remain in the linked studies below, without another duplicate review document.

### Candidate for the next mechanism test

**Status: executed; support failed.** [Whole-output transfer results](../topics/benchmarks/copy-cross-output-transfer-results.md) replace the design-only status below. The following records the pre-run rationale, not a queued experiment.

Checkpoint availability checked: same-seed 3767 cross-only/combined snapshots at updates 500, 1,000 and 6,000 match all six recorded replay hashes. No new model outputs were evaluated.

Candidate hypothesis: the complete cross-attention output carries a transferable signal that distinguishes continuing content from stopping in the successful combined-exposure model. Test the final update-6,000 pair first, where both fit the short task. Earlier snapshots are available, but should not become an automatic stage search.

One possible diagnostic is reciprocal replacement of the entire projected cross-attention output, including both heads, on identical source and decoder-prefix inputs. Keep the recipient residual and downstream computation. This avoids assuming that head indices have matching roles. For generated evaluation, compute the donor output from the recipient's current generated prefix, never from supplied future content or a separately generated donor prefix. Apply the same rule at every step without consulting the correct stopping time.

| Prediction | Interpretation if observed |
|---|---|
| Combined output improves weak full copying while preserving short copying and terminal EOS | Conditional sufficiency of the transferred cross-attention output package |
| Weak output harms combined full copying on the same inputs | Reciprocal sensitivity strengthens localization, subject to compatibility controls |
| Content improves but terminal EOS is lost | General stopping disruption; the proposed useful signal is not established |
| Both transfer directions damage short copying | Cross-model incompatibility limits interpretation; do not declare the package causal or irrelevant |

Same initialization does not guarantee compatible learned activation coordinates. Require self-transfer identity, native reconstruction, a magnitude-only control, and all short training/validation/test and long stopping outcomes. A magnitude control cannot eliminate every coordinate mismatch. Report donor/recipient norms and retain failures. Success would identify a transferable computation at the final checkpoints, not explain the optimizer history or prove a unique mediator of exposure.

The executed implementation supports arbitrary prefixes and terminal rows; the original fifth-token trace was not used unchanged. The [frozen protocol](../protocols/copy-cross-output-transfer.md) sets the metrics, controls and thresholds. No repeat is queued.

### Outcome: whole-output portability fails

At update 6,000, combined-to-weak output transfer gives 2/128 complete length-10 copies; the reverse gives zero. Both directions collapse ordinary short copying. Matching only the donor norm causes far less damage but does not repair the weak long failure. Thus the successful output is not directly portable into the other residual/downstream computation. Compatibility remains unresolved; the result neither isolates a learned mediator nor exonerates cross-attention. Native/self identities and all 112 reference cells pass.

Stop cross-model component transplants unless a new design addresses compatibility and distinguishes concrete alternatives. The exposure repair itself remains valid; its learning mechanism remains open. Full groups, stopping, norms and limitations are in the linked report.

## Evidence chain

### Continuing the same learned failure

[Matched exposure continuation](../topics/benchmarks/copy-exposure-continuation-results.md) starts both branches from the same weak update-6,000 weights, Adam state and generators. After 2,000 updates, added self-site exposure reaches 99/128 complete length-10 copies versus 55/128 under continued cross-only exposure, with 44 paired rescues and no harms. Every measured short group remains perfect. Length-8 stopping also improves relative to control.

Thus broader exposure can improve an already-learned weak solution beyond matched extra training. The 95% complete-repair gate still fails, with 29 early stops remaining. This identifies a conditional learning-intervention effect, not its internal mediator or a need for exposure from initialization. Both self-attention sites change together. Stop this continuation without another budget or stage search.

| Question | Evidence | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| Is early stopping the whole problem? | [Blocking early EOS](../topics/benchmarks/copy-stopping-results.md) leaves longer content failures | Changing the stopping decision is insufficient |
| Does removing EOS training repair content? | [Objective comparison](../topics/benchmarks/copy-eos-training-results.md) fails its required benefit | This objective intervention is not a reliable repair |
| Can this source format always encode length? | [Unmarked RoPE](../topics/benchmarks/copy-rope-results.md) has identical-value collisions across uniform-source lengths | A specific representation limitation, not impossibility for Transformers generally |
| Does an end marker resolve learning? | [Marked training](../topics/benchmarks/copy-marker-training-results.md) achieves reliable short copying, but weak longer copying | Available information alone does not ensure learned transfer |
| Is usable content still present? | [Supplied alignment](../topics/benchmarks/copy-marker-alignment-results.md) recovers complete longer copying | The saved model can use the content under an imposed route; this is not learned recovery |
| Where can an endpoint intervention help? | [Decoder-memory exclusion](../topics/benchmarks/copy-source-visibility-results.md) rescues all 351 first-token errors with the encoder unchanged | A local competing-read intervention is sufficient for first-token recovery |
| Do rankings fully identify failures? | [Saved scores](copy-learning-hypothesis.md) show outranking among both wrong and correct outputs | Ranking is informative but neither a complete cause nor a correctness test |
| Can training learn a repair without longer strings? | [Spaced-position training](../topics/benchmarks/copy-position-exposure-results.md): 100% full copying at lengths 8/10 in all three confirmation seeds | Broader positional exposure can repair tested transfer with unchanged architecture and short token streams |
| Which training site matters? | [Four-condition comparison](../topics/benchmarks/copy-position-sites-results.md): both 100% everywhere; cross-only fails in one seed; self-only stays weak | The combination meets the reliability rule; cross-only is sometimes sufficient |

The [broader content-length study](../topics/benchmarks/copy-length-exposure-results.md) also improved performance at an exposed length without solving longer extrapolation. That changed content exposure and should not be conflated with spacing position IDs on unchanged short strings. Each training comparison has its own matched controls. Historical scores across studies are not paired treatment estimates.

## What the learning intervention tells us

At a correct aligned source/decoder row, the relative position remains zero. Sampling spaced IDs broadens offsets to competing positions while retaining token count and labels. Under RoPE, the score contains `q? R_(r?p) k / ?d`.

[Ruoss et al. (2023), section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.16843v1#S3) supplies the existing sampling method. Our measurements test its local effect and site dependence. They do not establish novelty or predict other tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P[Choose positional-exposure sites] --> T[Train with matched short token streams]
    T --> W[Different learned parameters]
    W --> R[Measure attention rankings]
    W --> C[Measure generated full copying]
```

The joint changes in rankings and copying support the proposed training intervention. The diagram does not assume that rankings alone mediate copying. Some latest combined runs copy correctly despite an outranking head. The intervention site also differs from the location of learned changes: cross-attention gradients reach the encoder and other parameters.

## The weak cross-only seed: stopping versus content

[Saved-output localization and one controlled EOS intervention](../topics/benchmarks/copy-site-failure-results.md) narrow the failure. All 128 weak-seed test10 errors start with premature EOS at position 4 or 5. Suppressing EOS only during the known content length recovers 127 complete copies without supplied content or forced terminal EOS. One content substitution remains. Nine length-8 terminal-EOS failures persist.

This is a conditional inference repair, not a learned solution. It does not explain the training origin of the EOS preference. It also does not contradict earlier checkpoints where EOS suppression left widespread content errors. The declared full-recovery criterion fails; the bounded diagnostic is complete.

## Testing the direct end-position route

[Fixed-attention contribution removal](../topics/benchmarks/copy-end-route-results.md) rejects one immediate explanation: removing the direct end-position value rescues none of the weak model's 128 early-EOS failures and raises its EOS preference on every row. Three successful models instead lose all tested correct terminal decisions under removal while retaining correct content. This is conditional route dependence; distributed marker information and downstream interactions remain possible. The matched-size control has ineligible rows and extreme scaling, so it does not establish broad semantic specificity. The bounded diagnostic is complete.

## Holding the prefix fixed

[Paired six-to-ten-symbol source extension](../topics/benchmarks/copy-prefix-extension-results.md) keeps early source symbols, decoder prefixes and correct targets identical. At output position5, the weak model flips from correct content to EOS on every one of 128 pairs; three successful controls remain correct. Decoder position or prefix alone cannot explain this contrast. Suffix content, competitor count, contextual encoder states and marker relocation still change together, so the result does not establish pure length causality. The bounded comparison is complete.

## Excluding the added read positions

[Masking four added cross-attention positions](../topics/benchmarks/copy-added-read-mask-results.md) while preserving the complete long encoder rescues 17/128 weak-seed fifth-token predictions; 111 still select EOS. All successful-control groups remain perfect. The recovery criterion fails. Added reads have a local effect, but their exclusion does not broadly restore content decisions. Retained encoder context and marker position remain unchanged; weight renormalization prevents a pure competitor-count interpretation. No learning cause follows.

## When learning diverges

[Four exact historical replays](../topics/benchmarks/copy-learning-trajectory-results.md) recover 52 training snapshots. The weak seed reaches the frozen source-dependent failure signature at sampled update 1,000, before its first ordinary short-training fit at 2,000. No successful control meets that signature. Long EOS counts fluctuate and short fitting temporarily falls below its gate at 5,000. Thus the failure is present during early learning and persists through later short fitting; it is not supported as a purely late-stage deterioration. These reconstructed trajectories locate an observed divergence window, but do not identify a causal parameter change.

## Which developmental update package matters?

[Within-run update-500/update-1,000 swaps](../topics/benchmarks/copy-routing-development-results.md) show that cross-attention Q/K projections do not carry most of the weak seed's +7.750 extension-margin increase. Their conditional effects are +0.849 and -0.679; the remaining update package produces +8.429/+6.901. The rest-only hybrid emits EOS on all 128 long examples, but full short groups deteriorate even when paired-short answers survive. This rejects a simple Q/K-projection-only developmental account while leaving learned Q/K inputs, values and downstream processing coupled. Endpoint hybrids do not establish a training mechanism or repair.

## Intact computation during the same interval

[Tracing the unchanged snapshots](../topics/benchmarks/copy-intact-development-results.md) shows weak head 0 increasingly reads the short-source marker (52.3% to 99.7%) while its long-source read remains mixed (19.2% marker at update 1,000). Head 1 remains content-aligned. The paired cross-output difference and downstream final difference grow together, but common-position encoder distance decreases. The combined control also increases cross-output distance while reducing its extension margin. These observations identify a concrete routing/downstream pattern for a future controlled test; they do not allocate causal responsibility or explain the optimizer history.

## Testing the observed head pattern

[Transferring paired short-source head-0 weights](../topics/benchmarks/copy-head-pattern-transfer-results.md) at update 1,000 restores 128/128 weak long-source fifth-token answers from 2/128, with long values, head1 and downstream computation intact. Swapping marker and position-zero weights at identical entropy gives 0/128; all declared criteria pass. Controls suffer no mapped-answer harms, but their wrong-position permutation is nearly null. This supplies a sufficient local read-pattern intervention. It does not isolate marker weight from other pattern changes, measure generated copying/stopping, or explain why training learned the mismatch.

## Terminal supervision during the observed interval

[Matched continuation from update 500](../topics/benchmarks/copy-eos-development-results.md) changes only terminal-EOS loss during the next 500 updates. Native branches reproduce historical states exactly. The weak no-terminal branch restores all paired fifth-token answers and shrinks the head-0 marker gap mainly by reducing short-source concentration. This establishes training dependence on the objective term in this interval, but all omission branches lose proper length-10 stopping and the combined control loses content accuracy. Attention mediation remains unisolated; it is not a learned complete-copy repair.

## Retaining terminal learning at the classifier

[Classifier-only terminal gradients](../topics/benchmarks/copy-terminal-gradient-route-results.md) keep all targets but block new terminal feedback into earlier layers. All native continuations reproduce exactly. The intervention restores every fifth-token answer while failing complete long copying (0/0/2/0 out of 128) and short training fitting (train6: 0/0/8/0 out of 256). Thus the earlier loss-deletion failure is not avoided merely by retaining classifier EOS training in this interval. Gradient scope is verified; task mastery is not achieved. Both declared criteria fail, and no universal need for upstream feedback follows.

## Reliability and remaining limits

In the original completed positional-site comparison, every arm achieves 100% ordinary short train, validation and test accuracy and passes its declared layout-fit gate. This does not describe the later diagnostic continuations above. Yet cross-only seed 3767 achieves 92.97% at length 8 and 0% at length 10. Seeds 3779 and 3793 copy every random long example under cross-only. Adding self-site exposure repairs the observed weak seed; these successful cross-only seeds prevent a claim that both sites are universally necessary.

Remaining questions are specific:

- Which learned parameter changes explain the cross-only seed failure and its repair?
- Does the improvement survive other tasks, larger models or position ranges beyond those exposed during training?
- How much do encoder and decoder self-attention separately contribute? The latest self-site factor groups them together.

The current evidence does not answer those questions. It does answer a useful learning question: short training with narrow positional exposure can select a poor-transfer solution even when a matched exposure change permits success.

The two learning studies use fresh long examples within an already selected task distribution. Seeds within each study share a dataset; short pools are reused. Test IDs lie inside the sampled training range. Independent audits validate the tested numerical paths and results, not universal generalization or every training gradient.

**Stop this bounded copy comparison and retain its failures as well as successes.** No new position, head, seed or learning-rate sweep is queued. The [previous assessment](../../results/copy_position_sites/copy-assessment-before.md) preserves the earlier synthesis; individual reports retain all original measurements.

# Current research checkpoint

Completed, 2026-10-08: [shared-checkpoint exposure continuation](../topics/benchmarks/copy-exposure-continuation-results.md). From the identical weak update-6,000 model/Adam state, two matched 2,000-update branches retain full EOS supervision. Added self-site exposure reaches 99/128 length-10 complete copies versus cross-only continuation's 55/128: 44 rescues, zero harms. Length-8 counts are 128/128 versus 92/128. All short train/validation/test groups stay perfect at every measured checkpoint.

The effect is substantial but the 95% complete-repair gate fails: 29 intervention premature stops remain. Both branches improve over the original length-10 failure, so continuation alone also contributes. Exposure has a conditional effect from this saved state; its internal mediator, convergence and seed reliability remain unresolved. Failure does not prove exposure must begin early.

Verification: 4,000 updates, 638,000 examples, 3.36M targets; paired streams/generators, native starting scores, initialized evaluator/gradient checks and deliberate errors pass. Persisted audit covers 126 cells and 328 group rows within 1.434e-13; 129 protected files unchanged. Stop at update 8,000; no budget extension, component sweep or tuning is queued. Retention, state tracking and RL remain deferred. See [copy synthesis](copy-generalization-assessment.md) and [history](research-history.md).

This establishes that the saved models can decode the content under the supplied route. It does not establish why training failed to learn that route, or provide a usable learned repair. The earlier native failures remain valid.

## What counts as progress now?

One controlled change must improve a predefined held-out outcome while preserving the original task. An unsuccessful comparison is a valid completed result. One result document, one audit, one keep/reject decision. A threshold miss does not trigger tuning, new seeds or longer training.

# Research workflow

Purpose: understand Transformer computation, explain learned failures, and identify genuine gaps that could justify a new method. Toy-scale experiments can expose mechanisms and counterexamples; they cannot establish deployment superiority or field-level novelty by themselves.

The active goal is to identify failures and explain unresolved learning mechanisms. Follow the [mechanism agenda](assessments/learning-mechanism-agenda.md), starting from retention evidence. The [RL roadmap](topics/rl/rl-roadmap.md) is parked. Completed experiments retain their original budgets and conclusions; new explanatory questions require bounded designs.

The [checkpoint](assessments/research-checkpoint.md) is the current status. The [history](assessments/research-history.md) records earlier stages. This document defines the workflow, not an experiment queue.

## Choose a question

Start from a measured behavior or precise claim. Read existing evidence and the [failure register](assessments/failure-register.md) first. Name what a new result would distinguish. Prefer checkpoint inspection when training is unnecessary. An uncovered component alone is insufficient reason for a study.

| Question | Evidence required | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Is a mathematical statement true? | Derivation, assumptions and a counterexample search | The stated mathematical setting |
| Is code implementing the equations? | Independent outputs/gradients, boundary fixtures, deliberate errors | Tested implementations and inputs |
| What did a trained model learn? | Full fitting diagnostics, held-out groups, controlled interventions | Saved models, data and intervention conditions |
| Does an alternative help? | Adequate fitting, declared resource comparison, fresh paired confirmation | Tested tasks, budgets and seeds |

Arithmetic checks belong in reusable tests. Empirical and explanatory questions warrant studies. Neither test counts nor closed-study counts are progress measures by themselves.

Before selecting the next study, write a short gap assessment in the existing agenda: the exact model/task and failure, what local evidence and primary literature already answer, the unresolved claim, competing explanations, and a result that would distinguish them. Include what a negative result would teach. Do not promote a standard control into the research goal. If the gap is already answered or no discriminating result is available, stop or change the question before running.

Distinguish four questions: can the model represent the solution, can its actual write process produce it, can training find it, and does it transfer? A finite training-fit witness answers none of these universally. A novel method is a conditional outcome of this process, not a required conclusion.

## Develop, freeze, confirm

1. Check labels, baselines, evaluator/audit runtime, masks, missing groups and checkpoint reload. Use the [safe launcher](../tests/README.md) for archived copy tests.
2. If fitting is uncertain, declare a small recipe-development phase. Record every candidate; judge declared training-fit and selection metrics. Validation selection is allowed when declared. Keep confirmation data/seeds reserved.
3. Freeze the selected recipe, task, split, seeds, budgets, per-group metrics, error controls, meaningful improvement margin and stopping rule. If no candidate fits, report that outcome rather than silently launching a comparison.
4. Run fresh confirmation where an adoption claim requires it. Match initial values/data streams where applicable; disclose parameter, exposure and compute differences.
5. Audit results independently. Record observations, interpretations and unknowns separately. Preserve errors, failed criteria and valid earlier evidence.
6. Stop at the declared limit. Another run needs a distinct question and explicit bounded design.

## Compare resources honestly

Report parameters, updates, examples/tokens, effective batch, precision, context, hardware and peak memory. Equal parameters, equal tokens and equal compute are different comparisons. For timings, state warmup, synchronization, kernels and repeated samples; repeats are not independent training seeds.

Profile a complete optimizer step before increasing GPU budgets. Larger batches increase exposure at fixed updates. Eight GB of VRAM is a resource constraint, not evidence that a bigger run answers a better question.

## Interpret and improve

Check training fit before calling a failure generalization. Separate possible information paths from learned use, initialized identities from trained behavior, and diagnostic recovery from an implementable repair. Current findings can support a task-specific choice without identifying its cause.

A future architecture proposal needs a supported failure mechanism, explicit equations, comparison with primary predecessors, reproducible implementation and fresh evidence on the intended tasks/resources. Retain losing cases. No novel proposal or new training study is selected by this workflow.

Exact pre-cleanup wording is retained in the [maintenance snapshots](../results/maintenance_20261004/before.json). Those byte snapshots preserve provenance; their original relative links are not a navigation index.
